authorship: Milele Fit educational interpretation; role assignments remain coach-led.

positions.title: Loosehead prop
positions.job: Anchor the left of the front row, contribute to secure scrum ball, support lineout lifting and keep carrying, tackling and passing after set pieces.
positions.development: Develop stable force transfer and short-area movement alongside rugby technique. Scrum competence is judged in the assigned role by qualified coaches; a squat score cannot establish it.

positions.title: Hooker
positions.job: Connect the front row, strike for scrum possession, deliver lineout throws when assigned, and contribute to carries, tackles and breakdown work.
positions.development: Combine front-row control with repeatable throwing and movement between phases. Track throwing accuracy by target instead of hiding it inside a strength score.

positions.title: Tighthead prop
positions.job: Anchor the right of the front row, maintain effective scrum connection and contribute lifting, ball skills and repeated contact work around the field.
positions.development: Develop role-specific stability, force transfer and repeat effort. Tighthead and loosehead experience are assessed separately; switching sides is not automatic.

positions.title: Lock 4
positions.job: Connect the scrum unit, contribute to lineout possession as an assigned jumper or lifter, and arrive effectively at tackles, carries and breakdowns.
positions.development: Develop strength, movement, jump/lift coordination and repeated involvement. Record the actual lineout role; jersey 4 does not automatically mean jumper or caller.

positions.title: Lock 5
positions.job: Provide scrum connection, secure lineout work in the assigned role and contribute repeated carries, tackles and breakdown support.
positions.development: Develop force capacity and coordinated timing with the unit. Treat lock 4 and 5 as role assignments, rather than inventing different physical standards for each number.

positions.title: Flanker 6
positions.job: Connect set pieces to open play, tackle and reload, make sound breakdown decisions and offer carrying, handling and support around the field.
positions.development: Develop acceleration, braking, repeat effort and decision-making together. The coach defines blindside, openside and lineout responsibilities for this player.

positions.title: Flanker 7
positions.job: Contribute defensive pressure, legal possession contests, support play and repeated movement between the scrum, tackle and next phase.
positions.development: Develop quick arrival and controlled execution. Reaching the breakdown first is useful only when the player makes the right legal decision and can reload.

positions.title: Number 8
positions.job: Control possession at the scrum base, connect with 9, carry or distribute in open play and defend with repeatable work around the field.
positions.development: Develop base handling, short acceleration and force expression alongside scanning and choice. Judge the carry/pass decision separately from whether the contact was won.

positions.title: Scrum-half
positions.job: Connect forwards and backs, deliver usable ball, control tempo and decide when to distribute, carry or kick while organising the next phase.
positions.development: Develop service both ways, repeated repositioning and early scanning. Accurate passing from a stationary ball is the baseline; decisions and execution under changing pressure are separate skills.

positions.title: Fly-half
positions.job: Organise attacking shape and territory, read the defence and choose when to pass, carry or kick while communicating with the players around you.
positions.development: Develop distribution and decision-making at pace, supported by acceleration, movement control and reliable defence. Kicking distance alone does not measure game management.

positions.title: Winger · 11
positions.job: Finish chances near the touchline, support breaks, chase kicks and fulfil the assigned edge and backfield duties, including tackles and aerial contests.
positions.development: Develop acceleration and longer sprint speed, then practise using them with scanning, footwork and ball skills. Braking and turning matter when a kick, attacker or defensive picture changes.

positions.title: Inside centre
positions.job: Offer a direct carrying or second-playmaker threat, connect 10 to the wider attack and help maintain a connected defensive line.
positions.development: Develop the ability to fix a defender and make a usable pass as well as carry strongly. Physical capacity supports the role, while decisions determine when to use it.

positions.title: Outside centre
positions.job: Connect the midfield to the wing, read space at the defensive edge and create or exploit outside opportunities through running and passing.
positions.development: Develop acceleration and controlled changes of direction alongside defensive scanning and timing. A late read and slow movement can look similar but need different practice.

positions.title: Winger · 14
positions.job: Finish wide opportunities, stay available in support, chase kicks and carry out the assigned edge or backfield role on this side of the pitch.
positions.development: Develop speed with repeatable finishing, tracking and aerial skill. Test the assigned side and kicking duties; the two wings need not have identical responsibilities.

positions.title: Fullback
positions.job: Organise backfield coverage, secure kicks, choose counterattack or territory options and act as the final line of defence when a break occurs.
positions.development: Develop early positioning and communication with speed, braking and aerial control. Last-line defence is a reading-and-tracking task as well as a running task.
